summary: SSE session hysteresis after TLS renegotiation causes interleaved partial JSON fragments and missing closing brace
description:
Issue summary: Several OpenEdu Labs users report that long-running SSE streams occasionally deliver partial JSON objects at the tail of responses (duplicated fields in mid-object and missing trailing '}' ). The client sees a seemingly valid prefix, then a brief stream pause, then resumed fragments that interleave from a previous short-lived session. Impact: downstream consumer fails JSON parse and abandons the response 15-30% of affected streams during heavy outbound TLS rekeying windows. Environment: prod-us-east, customer using enterprise dedicated connection via corp-proxy that performs TLS interception and occasional renegotiation. Observed on model gptj-6b using streaming SSE path with keepalive interval 25s.

Observed behavior pattern:
- Stream starts and emits well-formed JSON chunks for ~30-90s.
- A short TLS rehandshake / renegotiation occurs at edge proxy (customer side).
- Post-renegotiation the SSE stream continues but occasional chunks are interleaved from an older ephemeral session: repeated keys (e.g., "delta": "..."), partial tokens, and final closing brace '}' is missing.

Why we care: This causes application-layer parse failure and a bad user experience in production classrooms (live transcript sessions drop).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Establish SSE streaming conversation against api.redwood.example with keepalive=25s using gptj-6b in us-east-1.
2) Simulate TLS interception/renegotiation on the client-side proxy (we used corporate BlueProxy v3 with midstream rekey).
3) Let stream run for ~45-120s and trigger renegotiation. Observe stream delivery: look for duplicated keys, interleaved partial fragments, or missing trailing '}' in final chunk.
4) Reproduce reliably on high-concurrency (>100 concurrent SSE) to increase probability.
logs: [2026-02-28T14:22:11.123Z] edge-proxy: TLS renegotiate from 192.0.2.45:4443 -> client connection id c-7f3a
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.210Z] api-gateway: SSE stream continue session_id s-98ad kv_snapshot=345 (keepalive ok)
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.218Z] serving-runtime: emit chunk -> '{"choices": [{"delta": "The capital of France is"',
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.355Z] client: JSON parse error: unexpected token '{' at offset 128 (missing closing brace)
workaround: Short-term workaround provided to customer: reduce client-side keepalive to 10s and enable explicit session pinning (pin model version + set max-sse-lifetime to 60s) to force tear-down and re-establish a clean session across proxy renegotiation windows. Also recommended to whitelist Redwood endpoints on corporate TLS interceptors to avoid midstream rekey where possible.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-28 15:10 - Support (Ava): Confirmed multiple incidents from OpenEdu Labs affecting long transcripts. Customer provided PCAPs showing midstream TLS rekey calls from their BlueProxy appliance.
2026-02-28 16:00 - SRE (Ravi): Checked API logs; server emits monotonically increasing sequence numbers for SSE events and keeps KV cache snapshots. No server-side crash observed at renegotiate time.

2026-02-28 16:18 - Eng (Maya): Hypothesis: When TLS renegotiation happens at the proxy we observe a short TCP session teardown on the ingress path; the gateway rebind attaches a new HTTP/1.1 session to the old logical SSE session which can cause out-of-order chunk reassembly in the presence of buffered writes at edge-proxy.\nEvidence: we saw two different connection ids within 200ms for the same client_id and overlapping sequence numbers.

2026-02-28 17:02 - Eng: Reproduced locally by enabling TLS rekey in a test proxy and observed interleaved write buffers: proxy replayed a small buffered packet from the pre-renegotiation connection after the post-renegotiation stream resumed.
impact_summary: Approximately 1200 streams from OpenEdu Labs in the last 24h, ~18% experienced parse failures; user-visible in live classroom transcripts. Customer escalated to enterprise success. Potentially broader impact for customers using TLS interception middleboxes.
next_steps: 1) Short-term: coordinate with customer to implement workaround (keepalive reduce + pin).

2) Medium-term: add defensive reassembly checks in api-gateway that detect session rebind / conn-id flip and inject an explicit SSE session reset event so clients can re-fetch final snapshot instead of silently resuming.
3) Long-term: harden edge-proxy buffered write semantics and ensure idempotent SSE chunk tagging with monotonic per-chunk UUID to allow dedupe on reconnects.
4) Engage Product Security to document guidance for customers with TLS interception appliances.
5) Create follow-up engineering task to prototype a session-reset patch: INT-2210 (linked).
resolution: In progress. Workaround shared and applied by customer (reduced keepalive). Engineering team drafted a gateway change to emit explicit SSE session-reset on connection-id transitions; patch submitted for review in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4712. Pending QA and canary deploy.
